A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity causes a defect in glucose transport activity in human skeletal muscle, which can be reversed with weight loss.
the defect in glucose transport activity in obesity is due to a defect in transporter activation and not to a defect in GLUT4 protein expression.
obesity contributes to whole-body insulin resistance through a defect in skeletal muscle insulin action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the defect in insulin action in obesity is not related to a defect in GLUT4 protein content in muscle.

the improvement in insulin responsiveness in skeletal muscles after weight loss is related to a significant increase in muscle glucose transport activity but not to changes in the levels of the glucose transport protein GLUT4.
the defect in glucose transport in skeletal muscle is reversible and that this may explain, at least in part, the improvement in whole-body glucose disposal that occurs with weight loss.
